lesson_title: How Do You Measure a Better Life?
hook_text: Norway's average income is about 145 times Malawi's. But does that number tell you who lives a good life?
clip_script: Imagine a cake that shows everything a country makes in a year. That is GDP. Now share it out: divide by the number of people and you get GDP per capita. South Africa: about 6 100 dollars a slice. Norway: about 87 000. Malawi: about 600. But wait. In real life the slices are not equal. South Africa has one of the most unequal splits in the world. So geographers count other things too. How long do people live? How many babies survive their first year? Can adults read? Do homes have clean water? Each number is like one mark on a report card. One mark never tells the full story. And some things no calculator can count: a grandmother raising children, a farmer feeding her family, the feeling of being safe. Measure many things, and always ask what the numbers hide.
visual_style: A cake cut into slices of very different sizes; a world map with GDP per capita labels; a report card with subject marks replaced by indicators; a calculator with a question mark over a family scene.
pacing: Brisk with the numbers, slowing for the closing question.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn how to calculate and interpret development indicators.
